content:
Since \(\pi\) maps \(A\) onto \(A\) and \(A\) is finite, \(\pi\) is a bijection, i.e. a permutation of the 6 elements.

The condition

\[
\pi(\pi(\pi(\pi(\pi(\pi(a))))))=a
\]

means

\[
\pi^6=\text{id}.
\]

For a permutation, this happens exactly when every cycle length divides \(6\). Thus the allowed cycle lengths are

\[
1,2,3,6.
\]

We count permutations of 6 elements whose cycle types use only these lengths.

The possible cycle structures and their counts are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Cycle type} & \text{Number} \\
\hline
1^6 & 1 \\
2\,1^4 & \binom{6}{2}=15 \\
2^2\,1^2 & \dfrac{6!}{2^2\cdot 2!\cdot 2!}=45 \\
2^3 & \dfrac{6!}{2^3\cdot 3!}=15 \\
3\,1^3 & \dfrac{6!}{3\cdot 3!}=40 \\
3^2 & \dfrac{6!}{3^2\cdot 2!}=40 \\
3\,2\,1 & \dfrac{6!}{3\cdot 2}=120 \\
6 & 5!=120
\end{array}
\]

Adding these:

\[
1+15+45+15+40+40+120+120=396.
\]

Therefore, the number of such functions is

\[
\boxed{396}
\]
